description: Every expansion: parameter operators, arithmetic, substitution, splitting and globbing.

cases.script:
diff <(printf "a
") <(printf "b
"); echo status=$?; paste <(seq 2) <(seq 3 4); comm <(printf "a
b
") <(printf "a
c
")

cases.name: expand: process substitution as input
cases.script:
while read l; do echo "got $l"; done < <(printf "x
y
"); wc -l < <(seq 3); grep -c a <(printf "a
a

cases.name: expand: process substitution as output
cases.script: printf "t1\nt2\n" | tee >(wc -l) >/dev/null; sleep 0.2; echo hi > >(tr a-z A-Z); sleep 0.2; echo done

cases.name: expand: process substitution path
cases.script: echo <(true) | grep -c "^/dev/fd/"; f() { cat "$1"; }; f <(echo via-function)

cases.name: expand: default and assign
cases.script: unset u; e=; echo "${u-a} ${u:-b} ${e-c} ${e:-d}"; echo "${u=x} $u"; echo "${e:=y} $e"

cases.name: expand: error operator
cases.script: unset u; ( : "${u?custom message}" ); echo status=$?; ( : "${u:?}" ) 2>/dev/null; echo status=$?

cases.name: expand: error operator on empty
cases.script: e=; ( echo "${e:?empty}" ); echo status=$?; echo "${e?not reached}" | wc -c

cases.name: expand: length
cases.script: s=héllo; a=(x yy zzz); echo ${#s} ${#a[@]} ${#a[1]} ${#undefined}

cases.name: expand: substring of arrays and positionals
expand: trim patterns
cases.script: p=/usr/local/lib/libfoo.so.1; echo ${p#*/} ${p##*/} ${p%.*} ${p%%.*} ${p#nomatch}

cases.name: expand: trim with brackets and classes
expand: replace with patterns and slashes
expand: replace on arrays
cases.script: a=(foo bar baz); echo ${a[@]/a/A} ${a[@]//a}; echo ${a[@]/#/-}

cases.name: expand: case modification
cases.script: w="hello world"; echo ${w^} ${w^^} ${w,} ; u=HELLO; echo ${u,,} ${u,} ${w^^o}

cases.name: expand: transform operators
cases.script: v="a b'c"; echo ${v@Q}; e='x\ty'; echo ${e@E}; declare -i n=3; echo ${n@a}; a=(1 2); echo ${a@A}; echo ${v@U} ${v@L} ${v@u}

cases.name: expand: prefix names
cases.script: abc1=1 abc2=2 abd=3; echo ${!abc*}; echo "${!abc@}"

cases.name: expand: array keys
cases.script: a=(x y z); a[7]=q; echo ${!a[@]}; declare -A m=([one]=1); echo ${!m[@]}

cases.name: expand: indirection
cases.script: target=value; ref=target; echo ${!ref}; arr=(a b); r2="arr[1]"; echo ${!r2}; unset nothing; n=nothing; echo "[${!n}]"

cases.name: expand: nested defaults
cases.script: unset a b; echo ${a:-${b:-deep}}; b=mid; echo ${a:-${b:-deep}}; echo "${a:-"quoted default"}"

cases.name: expand: unset in arithmetic and strings
cases.script: unset u; echo $((u + 1)) "[$u]"

cases.name: expand: arithmetic with variables and strings
expand: arithmetic errors
cases.script: echo $((1/0)); echo status=$?; echo $((2**-1)); echo status=$?; echo $((1+)); echo status=$?

cases.name: expand: command substitution strips trailing newlines
cases.script:
v=$(printf "a


"); echo "[$v]"; w=$(printf "

a"); echo "[$w]"

cases.name: expand: backquotes and nesting
cases.script: echo `echo a` $(echo $(echo b)) "$(echo "$(echo c d)")" `echo \`echo e\``

cases.name: expand: substitution reads a file
cases.script: echo content >/tmp/f; v=$(< /tmp/f); echo "$v"; v=$(</tmp/nosuch); echo status=$?

cases.name: expand: substitution status
cases.script: v=$(exit 3); echo $?; v=$(true; false); echo $?; x=$(echo ok) || echo no; echo $x

cases.name: expand: substitution in a subshell environment
cases.script: x=1; y=$(x=2; echo $x); echo $x $y; $(cd /tmp); pwd

cases.name: expand: default splitting
cases.script:
v="  a  b	c
 d "; set -- $v; echo $#; printf "[%s]" "$@"; echo

cases.name: expand: custom IFS
cases.script: IFS=:; v="a::b:c:"; set -- $v; echo $#; printf "[%s]" "$@"; echo

cases.name: expand: IFS mixing whitespace and delimiters
cases.script: IFS=" ,"; v=" a , b,,c "; set -- $v; echo $#; printf "[%s]" "$@"; echo

cases.name: expand: empty IFS disables splitting
cases.script: IFS=; v="a b c"; set -- $v; echo $#

cases.name: expand: quoted at and star
cases.script: set -- "a b" c; printf "[%s]" "$@"; echo; printf "[%s]" "$*"; echo; IFS=-; printf "[%s]" "$*"; echo; printf "[%s]" $*; echo

cases.name: expand: array star with IFS
cases.script: a=(x y z); IFS=,; echo "${a[*]}"; unset IFS; echo "${a[*]}"

cases.name: expand: empty and unset words vanish
expand: splitting results of substitution
cases.script: set -- $(printf "a b\nc"); echo $#; set -- "$(printf "a b\nc")"; echo $#

cases.name: expand: brace nesting and invalid forms
expand: brace with variables is literal
cases.script: n=3; echo {1..$n}; x=a,b; echo {$x}

cases.name: expand: glob basics
cases.script: cd /tmp; touch a1 a2 b1 .hidden; echo a*; echo ?1; echo [ab]1; echo [!a]1; echo *; echo nomatch*

cases.name: expand: glob ordering and dirs
cases.script: cd /tmp; mkdir -p d1/sub d2; touch d1/x d2/y; echo */; echo d*/*; echo ./d?

cases.name: expand: quoted globs are literal
cases.script: cd /tmp; touch star1; echo "star*" 'star*' star\*; v="star*"; echo $v "$v"

cases.name: expand: nullglob and failglob
cases.script: cd /tmp; shopt -s nullglob; echo x nomatch* y; shopt -u nullglob; shopt -s failglob; echo nomatch*; echo status=$?

cases.name: expand: dotglob
cases.script: cd /tmp; touch .dot vis; echo *; shopt -s dotglob; echo *

cases.name: expand: nocaseglob
cases.script: cd /tmp; touch Upper lower; shopt -s nocaseglob; echo u*; echo L*

cases.name: expand: extglob patterns
cases.script: shopt -s extglob; cd /tmp; touch a.txt b.log c.txt abc; echo *.@(txt|log); echo !(*.txt); echo +(a|b)c; echo ?(a)bc

stdout.text:
a.txt b.log c.txt
abc b.log
abc
abc

expected.reason: extended glob syntax always parses here, since the whole script is parsed before it runs; bash parses each line before running it, so enabling extglob on the same line is a syntax error there

cases.name: expand: extglob enabled on the same line
cases.script: shopt -s extglob; echo @(a|b)

expected.reason: extended glob syntax always parses here, since the whole script is parsed before it runs; bash parses each line before running it, so enabling extglob on the same line is a syntax error there

cases.name: expand: extglob off by default
cases.script: shopt -q extglob; echo status=$?; v=aaab; echo ${v##+(a)}

cases.name: expand: extglob patterns on a later line
cases.script:
shopt -s extglob
cd /tmp; touch a.txt b.log c.txt abc; echo *.@(txt|log); echo !(*.txt); echo +(a|b)c; echo ?(a)bc

cases.name: expand: extglob in conditions and case on a later line
cases.script:
shopt -s extglob
[[ abcabc == +(abc) ]] && echo plus; case x.tar.gz in *.@(gz|bz2)) echo compressed;; esac; v=aaab; echo ${v##+(a)}

cases.name: expand: extglob in conditions and case
cases.script: shopt -s extglob; [[ abcabc == +(abc) ]] && echo plus; case x.tar.gz in *.@(gz|bz2)) echo compressed;; esac; v=aaab; echo ${v##+(a)}

expected.reason: extended glob syntax always parses here, since the whole script is parsed before it runs; bash parses each line before running it, so enabling extglob on the same line is a syntax error there

cases.name: expand: globstar
cases.script: cd /tmp; mkdir -p g/a/b; touch g/1 g/a/2 g/a/b/3; shopt -s globstar; echo g/**; echo g/**/3

cases.name: expand: glob character classes
cases.script: cd /tmp; touch A1 b2 _3; echo [[:upper:]]*; echo [[:digit:]]* ; echo [[:alpha:]][[:digit:]]

cases.name: expand: GLOBIGNORE
cases.script: cd /tmp; touch keep drop.o; GLOBIGNORE="*.o"; echo *

cases.name: expand: glob after splitting
cases.script: cd /tmp; touch p1 p2; v="p* q"; echo $v

cases.name: expand: dollar quotes
cases.script: echo $'tab\there' $'\x41\u00e9' $'it\'s' $'\101' $'a\cA' | od -c | head -n 2

cases.name: expand: locale quotes
cases.script: echo $"translated" "$x"text

cases.name: expand: nested quotes in substitution
cases.script: echo "$(echo "inner \"quoted\"")"; echo "a${u:-"b c"}d"

cases.name: expand: backslash in double quotes
cases.script: echo "\$HOME \` \" \\ \a \n"

cases.name: expand: word joining
cases.script: a=x; echo "$a"y'$a'"$a"; echo ${a}_suffix $a_suffix

cases.name: expand: brace sequences at the ends of 64-bit integers
